key_insight: SparseDecoding aligns pruning with the model’s actual autoregressive decoding behavior, reducing the train-test mismatch that hurts pruned LLM accuracy.
engineering_relevance: By pairing decoding-aware pruning with an optimized sparse matrix-vector kernel, the method improves real inference latency where decoding is memory-bound.
method: Build calibration matrices from activations collected during dense-model generation, not from pre-collected natural text.
Prune with a Hessian-guided objective that matches decoding-time activation distributions.
Use a custom N:M SpMV kernel with bitmask indexing and fixed-step traversal for faster decoding.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, and Qwen3-14B/32B, showing better long-form generation performance and up to 1.48x end-to-end decoding speedup on A100 GPUs.
watch_item: The speedup depends on efficient sparse kernel support and hardware compatibility, so gains may be smaller if the deployment stack cannot exploit N:M sparsity well.
paper_title: SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference
